    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1746 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    TCU Coaching Candidates 2026: Identifying Potential Targets for Horned Frogs Coaching Search

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that it’s time for another TCU Horned Frogs coaching search, with the program looking for someone to turn things around after a disappointing 2026 season.
    • Let’s dive into our TCU coaching candidates to replace Sonny Dykes.
    • There’s a very real possibility that the TCU coaching search will focus on in-state options with head-coaching experience.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that it’s time for another TCU Horned Frogs coaching search, with the program looking for someone to turn things around after a disappointing 2026 season. After head-coaching stability for more than two decades under Gary Patterson, the Horned Frogs will be looking for their third head football coach since 2022.

    Let’s dive into our TCU coaching candidates to replace Sonny Dykes.

    There’s a very real possibility that the TCU coaching search will focus on in-state options with head-coaching experience. Those are two things that should put Texas State Bobcats head coach G.J. Kinne near the top of the program’s list. Kinne bounced around as quarterbacks coach at Hawai’i (2020) and UCF (2021) before landing his first head-coaching job at Incarnate Word, immediately delivering a 12-2 record with a trip to the FCS Semifinals. That success landed him at Texas State, where he had a lot of work to do given the football program went a combined 13-35 in four seasons with Jake Spavital. Kinne immediately doubled the Bobcats’ win total year-to-year, and he’s won at least seven games in each of his four seasons at the helm with the offense ranking seventh in scoring (38.7 PPG) this season. Kinne’s roots are in Texas, and the combination of his track record of winning with two different programs paired with his offensive mind make him an ideal option for TCU.

    If there’s a favorite to be the next TCU football coach, it might be Jeff Traylor. The 58-year-old started at the high school level, first as an assistant and then taking over as the head coach at Gilmer High School. The success there got him a job on the Texas Longhorns coaching staff (2015-16) coaching special teams, followed by stops at SMU (2017) and Arkansas (2018-19) on the offensive side of the ball. UTSA, having gone 7-17 in the final two years under Frank Wilson, took a chance on Traylor. The Roadrunners immediately took off with a seven-win season in Traylor’s first year as a head coach, followed by consecutive campaigns with double-digit wins. At UTSA, Traylor is on the verge of another 10-win campaign with a potential American Conference Championship title to go with it. He won state titles as a high school coach and has taken UTSA’s football program to latest heights. At TCU, Traylor could eventually get the Horned Frogs into the College Football Playoff.

    Recent findings suggest that the primary focus with our TCU coaching candidates centers on those who have experience being a head coach. That’s partly due to the fact that there aren’t a ton of appealing coordinators right now who are worth taking a chance on. Miami Hurricanes play-caller Shannon Dawson is an exception. He’s helped elevate quarterback Darian Mensah into being a likely Heisman Trophy finalist in 2026, with the Hurricanes offense being one of the biggest reasons why they’ll make the playoff in consecutive seasons. Dawson also has some familiarity with coaching in Texas, having served on the Houston Cougars coaching staff from 2019-2022. Dawson would be a bit of a riskier hire, but there’s also the opportunity that the Horned Frogs strike gold with a brilliant mind who can lead a perennial Big 12 Conference contender.

    According to recent reports, relationships matter in a coaching search. TCU athletic director Mike Buddie decided to make a head-coaching change just months after signing Dykes to a contract extension. Buddie was Army’s athletic director when Monken led the school to a 12-2 record. It’s fair to wonder in a situation like that if the person overseeing the Horned Frogs coaching search already has someone in mind. It’s been a disappointing 2026 season for the Army Black Knights, who could potentially fail to win six games for the first time since 2019. Monken, age 59, may now realize he’s taken this program as far as it can go given the constraints that come with being the head coach of an academy school. He’d have far more resources available to him at TCU than he ever did as head coach at either Army or Georgia Southern. Given he’ll be 60 years old in April, this hire would also fall in line with the Horned Frogs’ recent history with head coaches.

    In a recent development, zach Kittley had his work cut out for him when he agreed to become the head coach at Florida Atlantic University. The FAU Owls gave Willie Taggart a shot and bailed on that after three seasons (15-18 record) only for things to get even worse under Tom Herman (6-16). Kittey had to overhaul everything in 2025, leading to just a one-win improvement. This season has offered a far better glimpse of what he’s capable of when he brings in the players he wants and there starts to be cohesion in the system. FAU (7-4) has delivered its best record since the Lane Kiffin years, with the Owls’ passing game (326.7 pass ypg) leading to one of the highest-scoring offenses in the nation. If Kittley can turn Caden Veltkamp from a quarterback who threw 17 interceptions from 2024-25 into a highly-efficient passer (33-6 TD-INT and 70% completion rate), imagine what he could do with an even better quarterback and supporting cast at TCU.

    #130954. North Korea's Kim calls for nuclear arsenal expansion, says status 'will never change'

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (465 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    North Korea's Kim calls for nuclear arsenal expansion, says status 'will never change'

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (465 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for bolstering the country's nuclear arsenal and expanding the use of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains, state media reported Thursday, as Pyongyang reaffirmed its determination to retain its nuclear arms.
    • Kim's comments followed a working visit Wednesday to facilities involved in nuclear material production and weapons research, according to the Korean Central News Agency.
    • At the Nuclear Weapons Institute, he urged greater attention to "operationalizing" tactical nuclear weapons for a range of missions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for bolstering the country's nuclear arsenal and expanding the use of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains, state media reported Thursday, as Pyongyang reaffirmed its determination to retain its nuclear arms.

    Kim's comments followed a working visit Wednesday to facilities involved in nuclear material production and weapons research, according to the Korean Central News Agency.

    At the Nuclear Weapons Institute, he urged greater attention to "operationalizing" tactical nuclear weapons for a range of missions.

    Kim directly linked the development of those weapons to North Korea "sharing a border with its most dangerous, hostile state," an apparent reference to South Korea.

    According to recent reports, the visit was part of Pyongyang's efforts to counter what Kim described as "the reckless expansion of adversary states' nuclear forces and military alliances," according to KCNA. He also singled out South Korea as a threat to North Korea's security and sovereignty.

    Kim reiterated that North Korea's status as a nuclear-armed state was irreversible, dismissing "denuclearization rhetoric" and saying its nuclear status "will never change.".

    "[Our nuclear policy] is a core element of safeguarding the sovereignty of the Republic, enshrined in the supreme law of the state," he added.

    The report did not identify the sites Kim visited or disclose any production figures.

    The announcement followed an assessment last week by the International Atomic Energy Agency that another extension to Yongbyon's original uranium-enrichment facility had been externally completed by late October.

    The nuclear watchdog has lacked access to North Korea since 2009 and monitors its activities using satellite imagery and open-source intelligence.

    In a recent development, citing what he portrayed as growing threats from Washington and its allies, Kim accused the U.S. of encouraging neighboring allies to acquire nuclear-powered submarines, pursuing nuclear sharing and the joint use of nuclear weapons.

    Recent findings suggest that his comments come after South Korea announced efforts to acquire nuclear-powered submarines after President Donald Trump backed the plan in October 2025, according to a White House joint fact sheet. Nuclear-powered propulsion does not itself mean that a vessel carries nuclear weapons.

    Trump had expressed interest in meeting with Kim at the APEC summit in Shenzhen last week, according to Reuters, but no meeting took place and North Korea did not publicly respond to the proposal.

    Trump denied that Kim had ignored him, adding that communications could "start up right away," in an interview with the New York Post Tuesday. He remarked the two leaders had not been in contact "recently.".

    "We've been off to other things," Trump added.

    North Korea has continued to accelerate its nuclear weapons development and rebuff South Korean and U.S. attempts to resume dialogue since negotiations between Trump and Kim collapsed in 2019.

    — CNBC's Jenny Lee contributed to this report.

    In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The firm reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper announced a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Recent findings suggest that following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the organization delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key update was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Sources indicate that given the recently announced base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    In a recent development, bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the manufacturer's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    According to recent reports, bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the organization increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Recent findings suggest that gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and plans to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," said the analyst.

    Gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The organization announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    According to recent reports, in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier stated that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    In a recent development, he noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • South Korean beauty stocks jumped Thursday as the country's skincare brands dominated Amazon's bestseller rankings ahead of Black Friday.
    • Shares of K-beauty giant APR climbed 3.77%, while cosmetic contracts manufacturers Kolmar Korea and Cosmax gained 5.46% and 2.91%, respectively.
    • APR shares, in particular, have rallied sharply this week, up 28%, defying a broader market sell-off in Seoul markets, with the benchmark Kospi index down 2.65% during the same period.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korean beauty stocks jumped Thursday as the country's skincare brands dominated Amazon's bestseller rankings ahead of Black Friday.

    Shares of K-beauty giant APR climbed 3.77%, while cosmetic contracts manufacturers Kolmar Korea and Cosmax gained 5.46% and 2.91%, respectively.

    APR shares, in particular, have rallied sharply this week, up 28%, defying a broader market sell-off in Seoul markets, with the benchmark Kospi index down 2.65% during the same period.

    A cosmetic sector index tracked by Meritz Securities had gained 12% this week until Wednesday, according to a Thursday note from the brokerage.

    The rally reflects renewed optimism over earnings growth following strong performances by K-beauty brands across major e-commerce platforms in the U.S. and Europe with Black Friday sales already underway, as well as increasingly attractive valuations following months of share price declines, according to Meritz.

    K-beauty products topped Amazon's skincare bestseller rankings across six major markets — the U.S., the U.K., Germany, France, Spain and Italy — as of Nov. 25, according to data compiled by Meritz Securities. Other Korean beauty brands, including Biodance, Illiyoon and Anua, also ranked among the top 10 in the U.S., the data demonstrated.

    As of Thursday morning, Korean beauty products occupied several of the top spots in Amazon's U.S. beauty and personal care category, the e-commerce website revealed.

    Meritz Securities expects APR shares to maintain their positive momentum through the year-end, with a more substantial rebound in early 2027.

    It has been revealed that the brokerage named APR and Cosmax as its top picks in the cosmetics sector. Korean beauty brands have established an "overwhelming presence" in the bestseller rankings of major e-commerce platforms during Black Friday sales, prompting the market to reassess the growth's potential, the brokerage remarked.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • In a recent development, the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    In a recent development, the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo stated. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    It has been revealed that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The organization posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Recent findings suggest that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo noted.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    #130941. Industry News: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm states

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (683 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm states

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu mentioned.
    • In a recent development, xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu mentioned. "Technology is moving at a much faster clip.".

    In a recent development, xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday. The tech giant looks to start training the robot as a store assistant in its retail car locations in the first quarter next year, after starting mass production in January. Sales are set to begin in the second quarter, with deliveries expected later in the year.

    Founded in 2014 as an electric car firm, Xpeng beat Tesla to rolling out driver-assist in mainland China. The Chinese automaker has launched its own artificial intelligence chips. It's also expanded into personal flying vehicles and robotics. The robotics unit this summer raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in its first funding round, led by IDG Capital.

    Investors, however, appear to be a tad skeptical about the developments at Xpeng, with the downturn in the Chinese auto market also weighing on the company. Xpeng's shares, listed in both New York and Hong Kong, have dropped more than 55% this year amid broad sector declines.

    China's humanoid industry has faced more regulatory scrutiny on financing in recent months after Unitree's high-profile IPO and stock slump, as well as a rush of capital into the sector. That's all raised questions about commercialization and the efficacy of the core tech.

    Gu remarked Xpeng's robotics stands out for its rare combination of the hardware, software and real-life use cases. He's expecting to add more investors after Iron's planned commercial launch next year.

    Sources indicate that "You can always make the head talk, you can always make the leg run, you can always make the hands to do certain tasks," Gu remarked. "But doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part. And then doing everything well, not falling down, not getting distracted. The model has to work in sync.".

    Most humanoid robot startups, especially in China, focus on a portion of the tech, such as hands or the artificial intelligence-powered brain. Some in the industry also see themselves as original equipment manufacturers, with another manufacturer tying the parts together for the finished robot.

    But that may be easier said than done.

    In a recent development, xpeng's co-founder and CEO He Xiaopeng, a software engineer, always thought that software could solve "everything,'" Gu said. "And after he got into the EV business he realized how hard it is to make hardware ... really do the things that you want to do safely and consistently.".

    On Wednesday, Xpeng announced its "Turing Physical AI Architecture" for using AI and real-time decision-making tech to control cars and humanoids.

    Gu told CNBC that Xpeng's robotics development only needs the driver-assist chips, which the tech giant already has, indicating limited impact from U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip sales to China.

    "Right now we don't see any change to our supply chain, and also ability to have these chips.".

    In 2023, Xpeng's then-head of autonomous driving, Xinzhou Wu, left to lead Nvidia's automotive chip business.

    As Xpeng ramps up its humanoid robotics business, Gu noted the firm's existing work in autonomous driving technology translates easily to a new product line — with far higher profit margins. "It's much easier to be profitable for the robotics business than the autos business.".

    Robotics will likely become a meaningful part of Xpeng's business in two to three years, Gu said, with profitability coming as soon as next year. That value will "dramatically" increase with robots entering households, he said.

    But Gu noted that compared to commercial environments, homes require robots to act safely around elderly people, children and pets, in addition to reacting to emergency situations. That increases requirements for battery power and performance consistency, he stated.

    #130940. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (741 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm.
    • Industry observers note that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Industry observers note that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously unveiled commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider noted in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    It has been revealed that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    In a recent development, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The tech giant had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, remarked CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    Recent findings suggest that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he stated in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any significant changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real problem is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Massive companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he noted. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
    • Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the major positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
    • In a recent development, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the major positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    In a recent development, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the latest year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    According to recent reports, emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    Sources indicate that “Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another key player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    According to recent reports, the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Recent findings suggest that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    According to recent reports, it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    In a recent development, PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

    Sources indicate that after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    In a recent development, both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

    Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

    According to recent reports, 💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

    Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

    PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

    Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

    Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

    Industry observers note that not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    Recent findings suggest that one final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    It has been revealed that the ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

    Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    Sources indicate that aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a massive chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

    Sources indicate that cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

    Sources indicate that mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

    It has been revealed that other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

    Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

    On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth massive chance of the night. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

    Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

    McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

    We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

    Recent findings suggest that some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg.     It has been revealed that what will we learn from the “newly introduced Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    Industry observers note that unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    Sources indicate that I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    Industry observers note that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    According to recent reports, aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a massive summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    “I feel like the club is in a newly introduced era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    It has been revealed that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    Recent findings suggest that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    #130936. Judge blocks FCC early-renewal process for Disney-owned ABC stations, for now

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (400 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Judge blocks FCC early-renewal process for Disney-owned ABC stations, for now

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (400 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A judge has temporarily blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing its early renewal of a set of broadcast station licenses for Disney-owned ABC.
    • District Court in Washington granted Disney the preliminary injunction it sought and denied the FCC's attempt to dismiss the suit.
    • Industry observers note that "This is not a close case," wrote the federal judge.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A judge has temporarily blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing its early renewal of a set of broadcast station licenses for Disney-owned ABC.

    Judge Loren L. AliKhan of U.S. District Court in Washington granted Disney the preliminary injunction it sought and denied the FCC's attempt to dismiss the suit.

    Industry observers note that "This is not a close case," wrote the federal judge. "Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face—loss of their broadcast licenses—the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness.".

    Sources indicate that the broadcast network had filed the lawsuit and followed the FCC beginning its early review of the ABC licenses. The government agency cited concerns around ABC's diversity, equity and inclusion efforts as the reason behind the start of the early renewal — years ahead of their scheduled expiration.

    "Today's decision is an important victory for the First Amendment," stated an ABC spokesperson.

    An FCC spokesperson said in a statement that the part of the decision granting ABC's motion "is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law," the Associated Press reported.

    In her ruling, AliKhan said that early license renewal proceedings came over a year into the FCC's enforcement push against ABC, starting with an investigation into Disney's employment practices in March 2025 and leading to the renewal proceedings in April this year.

    ABC on Tuesday had said that it continued to "face irreparable harm" from the administration, which "has been acting" through the FCC, which is run by President Donald Trump appointee Brendan Carr.

    AliKhan, a Joe Biden appointee, noted in her ruling that ABC had to change how it handled guest appearances for top indicates "The View" and "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" with no candidate for public office appearing on the former and a senatorial candidate's appearance on the latter uploaded to YouTube instead of being broadcast.

    "The prospect of license non-renewal has also factored into plaintiffs' calculus of when and how they cover President Trump and political topics," remarked the judge.

    ABC had alleged that Trump and Carr have been making comments "intended to chill their protected speech," and that such comments have escalated since the 2024 presidential election.

    The White House and the FCC didn't immediately respond to requests for comment from CNBC.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to the story.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (465 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    How Trump’s latest tariff moves hand India an edge over rival Asian exporters

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (465 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the latest U.S.
    • The Office of the United States Trade Representative has proposed a tariff of 17% on Indian exports if Upcoming Delhi "were to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade" with Washington.
    • Meanwhile, the USTR has proposed tariffs of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Thailand, and 20% on China and Vietnam, subject to their respective trade deals, handing India a competitive advantage over rival exporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the latest U.S. tariff rates unveiled Wednesday have signaled that Washington is willing to offer India an edge over its competitors if Fresh Delhi agrees to finalize a long-pending trade deal.

    The Office of the United States Trade Representative has proposed a tariff of 17% on Indian exports if Upcoming Delhi "were to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade" with Washington. It added that without a trade deal, India could face tariffs of up to 25% under Section 301 investigations encompassing excess production capacity that harms U.S. interests.

    Meanwhile, the USTR has proposed tariffs of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Thailand, and 20% on China and Vietnam, subject to their respective trade deals, handing India a competitive advantage over rival exporters.

    The U.S. expects the announcement of a lower tariff rate will encourage Latest Delhi to sign off on a trade deal before the G20, Atman Trivedi, partner at Washington-based DGA Albright Stonebridge Group, told CNBC.

    India has got a "better bargain with Washington than its main competitors," and it may be enough for the Indian government "to declare victory and secure domestic backing for the deal," Trivedi mentioned.

    In February, U.S. President Donald Trump had declared a deal with India, claiming that Upcoming Delhi had accepted to "Buy American" at a much higher level after the U.S. agreed to slash tariffs to 18% from 50% earlier.

    The India-U.S. trade deal has been pending with both sides indicating there was little room to grant concessions, while the Supreme Court annulling Trump tariffs allowed Newly introduced Delhi to demand preferential tariffs that give it an edge over competitors.

    Recent findings suggest that "Today's announcement increases the urgency of reaching an agreement," Ronak D. Desai, visiting fellow at Hoover Institution, Stanford University, told CNBC. He added that while the prospect of a 17% tariff may strengthen the economic case for the deal, the threat of a 25% tariff could stir the sensitivity of the Indian government.

    "The Modi government will be particularly sensitive to any perception that India is conceding under American Pressure," Desai said.

    According to recent reports, india's commerce ministry on Wednesday said it "does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," denying the findings of the USTR investigation, but added that it remains committed to "working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement.".

    Despite India facing steep tariffs, which were raised to 50%, Latest Delhi's trade surplus with the U.S. rose to $57.3 billion in 2025 from $45.2 billion in 2024.

    Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Trump are likely to meet in December for the G20 leaders' meeting in Florida, and several experts believe the two leaders could seal the trade deal on the sidelines of the summit.

    #130930. Vance claims he was assured Jensen Huang was not under DOJ investigation

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (681 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Vance claims he was assured Jensen Huang was not under DOJ investigation

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vice President JD Vance noted Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche told him Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation.
    • "I was told by the Department of Justice and multiple officials in our national security apparatus that he was under no investigation," Vance told reporters in Ohio on Wednesday after being asked what assurances he had gotten that Huang was not under investigation.
    • Vance spoke two days after President Donald Trump told CNBC in an interview that an investigation had been done.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vice President JD Vance noted Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche told him Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation.

    "I was told by the Department of Justice and multiple officials in our national security apparatus that he was under no investigation," Vance told reporters in Ohio on Wednesday after being asked what assurances he had gotten that Huang was not under investigation. "Not even that he was about to be prosecuted; that he's under no investigation.".

    Vance spoke two days after President Donald Trump told CNBC in an interview that an investigation had been done.

    Trump was asked what Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws.

    "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump mentioned Monday.

    Reuters reported Wednesday that the Department of Justice did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before Trump pushed for his reinstatement as CEO.

    Blanche had concluded there was no evidence Huang had broken any laws based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed, according to the report.

    Industry observers note that the DOJ did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Reuters report. And the White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Vance saying Huang was under no investigation when Trump had said there was one. Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about Vance's remarks.

    Blanche on Tuesday dodged questions about whether there had been an investigation.

    "What the president noted is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him," Blanche said after being asked whether the DOJ had investigated Huang and, if so, what were the results of the probe.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday, after the chipmaker's board of directors said it had received "input from senior levels of the United States government" that Huang was not a national security risk. Trump took credit for Huang's reinstatement in the interview with CNBC shortly after Nvidia's announcement.

    Huang resigned following The Fresh York Times reporting multiple affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing and who was an executive for the Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed.

    It has been revealed that the reporting added fuel to allegations that Nvidia should have known its artificial intelligence chips were being diverted to China and being used by Chinese companies, violating U.S. export laws.

    "The product they create is a very crucial part of us staying ahead of the SI arms race with China. We really do care about ensuring those chips do not fall into the wrong hands," Vance said, using the Trump administration's preferred acronym for AI, which the president calls "super intelligence.".

    "We actually see this is an opportunity for Nvidia to focus on complying with American export controls, and we think Jensen Huang is going to take that very seriously," Vance continued.

    "We received the assurances that he was not under any significant — he was under no investigation — and the accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence," Vance remarked.

    On Tuesday, Trump left the door open to pardon Huang in an interview with the Upcoming York Post, but Vance said on Wednesday that the CEO doesn't need one.

    Sources indicate that "I don't think he needs a pardon at all," Vance said. "I haven't seen any evidence again that he committed a crime. And if there is evidence that he committed a crime, then that's up to relevant authorities to actually bring a prosecution against him.".

    Industry observers note that huang is scheduled to appear for a closed-door interview with House committees about his dealings with Megaspeed on Tuesday. At the same time, Nvidia will hold its annual conference where it showcases new technology in Washington.

    — Kevin Breuninger contributed to this report.

    U.S. proposes upcoming tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the U.S.
    • According to recent reports, the administration rolled out those and other trade investigations in March, weeks after the Supreme Court unraveled a major piece of President Donald Trump's tariff-heavy economic policy by striking down his "liberation day" duties.
    • The latest action targets foreign economies that create, sustain or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors that the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the U.S. is preparing upcoming tariffs on 14 economies, including China, the EU, Japan and India, following investigations into what the Trump administration says are excess manufacturing practices that disadvantage U.S. commerce.

    According to recent reports, the administration rolled out those and other trade investigations in March, weeks after the Supreme Court unraveled a major piece of President Donald Trump's tariff-heavy economic policy by striking down his "liberation day" duties. Trump has since been accused by critics of his tariffs of trying to revive the canceled duties using other legal authorities.

    The latest action targets foreign economies that create, sustain or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors that the U.S. finds unreasonable and burdensome or restrictive to its commerce, a senior U.S. official told reporters Tuesday evening.

    The new tariffs are "targeted," not blanket rates, and will vary for each economy, and many will not exceed the rates established in previously reached trade deals, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the forthcoming duties.

    In a recent development, the rates, which mostly range from 15% to 20%, are "not really additive" and generally will not stack on top of existing duties, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" Wednesday morning.

    Industry observers note that "In effect, it'll look more like a top up," Greer noted. "When it all nets out, it really will just top up a few percentage points.".

    Industry observers note that an exception is China, which faces a 20% rate under the upcoming tariff policy, "so it will go up some," Greer said. But at the same time, both countries are moving to remove tariffs on some of each other's goods in what Greer called "stability-generating activity through this action.".

    Sources indicate that the senior U.S. official said Tuesday that the 20% rate will come on top of the so-called forced technology transfer-related tariffs of roughly 25%, which were implemented during Trump's first presidential term. U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods will therefore reach about 45%, give or take for different goods, the official said.

    Recent findings suggest that average U.S. tariffs rates on Chinese goods stood at about 36.5% as of July, according to the Congressional Research Service.

    Greer also said on CNBC that the newly introduced policy likely will not take effect for months.

    In a recent development, "We've talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we're proposing," he said. "I think a lot of this is baked in, and I don't think any of these would actually take effect earlier than a couple months from now.".

    The administration says the tariffs target what it calls "overcapacity" — excess industrial production, often supported by government subsidies, that allows cheaper goods to flood global markets and undercut U.S. producers.

    According to recent reports, china has disputed the allegations. "The so-called 'overcapacity' does not really exist," China's foreign ministry remarked Wednesday before the official reports were released by the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, according to Reuters.

    Recent findings suggest that the overcapacity levies are being imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The Trump administration invoked the same statute to launch investigations into 60 economies over alleged forced-labor complications.

    Those investigations, which also began in March, led to broad tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on goods from dozens of countries covering 99.4% of U.S. imports.

    The Section 301 actions came weeks after the Supreme Court struck down the near-global tariffs that Trump had enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

    Shortly after the court's ruling, Trump invoked Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 to impose a 10% global tariff. That tariff expired after 150 days, and was immediately replaced with the forced-labor-related duties.

    An ongoing lawsuit accuses the Trump administration of citing forced-labor concerns as a "pretext" in pursuit of reviving Trump's worldwide tariff regime.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Taking on Starlink: Europe’s largest satellite factory opens in push to rival Musk

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (438 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the largest satellite factory in Europe was inaugurated in Belgium this week, boosting the continent's efforts to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink and reduce reliance on U.S.
    • Privately held Belgian satellite manufacturer Aerospacelab secured a 2.4-billion-euro ($2.6 billion) contract in September to manufacture 264 of the 348 satellites planned for IRIS², the European Union's answer to SpaceX's Starlink business.
    • Aerospacelab noted this will "form the backbone of Europe's sovereign, secure, and resilient connectivity infrastructure by 2030." It will be named Ectro from Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the largest satellite factory in Europe was inaugurated in Belgium this week, boosting the continent's efforts to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink and reduce reliance on U.S. space infrastructure.

    Privately held Belgian satellite manufacturer Aerospacelab secured a 2.4-billion-euro ($2.6 billion) contract in September to manufacture 264 of the 348 satellites planned for IRIS², the European Union's answer to SpaceX's Starlink business.

    Aerospacelab noted this will "form the backbone of Europe's sovereign, secure, and resilient connectivity infrastructure by 2030." It will be named Ectro from Nov. 30.

    Its new oval-shaped, 20,000-square-meter facility in southern Belgium, inaugurated by Belgian King Philippe, will be able to produce up to 500 satellites annually, which would make it the world's third-largest satellite production site, according to the Belgian royal palace.

    Employees are expected to move into the megafactory in January, and production is slated to begin by the end of 2028, according to AFP.

    Satellite connectivity has become increasingly notable to everyday life as well as national security.

    It provides internet access to remote locations and defense equipment like warships and fighter jets, and lets governments and militaries communicate securely where Earth-based networks are unavailable or disrupted.

    The importance of such capabilities has become particularly apparent in Ukraine, as the country's military relies heavily on Starlink connectivity to fight Russian forces. Recent restrictions to the service over Russian-occupied territory reported by Ukrainian officials further underscored the way geopolitical conflict may depend on commercial businesses.

    But Europe still has a long way to go in challenging Starlink's dominance.

    SpaceX claims it has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in low Earth orbit, making it by far the largest satellite constellation in the world, and looks up to 100,000 satellites.

    Among the challengers is Amazon, whose satellite business, Amazon Leo, has deployed over 400 satellites and aims an initial in-orbit constellation of more than 3,200.

    Meanwhile, French Eutelsat operates more than 600 satellites in low Earth orbit through its OneWeb constellation. The tech giant is also part of the SpaceRISE consortium alongside SES and Hispasat, tasked with developing and operating IRIS².

    The European Commission has called IRIS² a "strategic asset to achieve space sovereignty in the face of commercial satellite constellations, such as Starlink." The aim is for first launches to take place by the end of 2029, with initial services expected soon after.

    In August, the Commission and SpaceRISE consortium announced they were expanding the main constellation from 282 to 348 satellites, increasing its secure communications capacity for EU governments by 60%.

    Defense and security applications were the main drivers of the expanded scope, the Commission remarked.
